title: Coarse descent from a categorical quotient of a Zariski torsor presentation
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G$ be a group scheme over $k$ (a scheme with multiplication, unit and inverse satisfying the group identities), and let $J$ be a $k$-scheme with a left $G$-action [def-pc-scheme]. A Zariski locally trivial $G$-torsor over $T$ means a $T$-scheme $E$ with $G_T$-action admitting a Zariski open cover of $T$ on which it is equivariantly isomorphic to $G\times_k T$ acting on itself by left multiplication. Let $\mathcal F$ be a category fibred in groupoids over $k$-schemes [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], equipped with a cartesian equivalence $e$ to the fibred groupoid whose objects over $T$ are pairs $(E\to T,u:E\to J)$ with $E$ such a torsor and $u$ equivariant; arrows are equivariant torsor isomorphisms commuting with $u$, and pullback is scheme fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $Q$ be a $k$-scheme and $q:J\to Q$ a $G$-invariant morphism. Suppose that for every algebraic space $B/k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] composition with $q$ is a bijection from $k$-maps $Q\to B$ to $G$-invariant maps $J\to B$, and for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] it induces $J(\Omega)/G(\Omega)\simeq Q(\Omega)$. Here invariance means equality after composition with the action and the projection $G\times_k J\rightrightarrows J$, and the quotient of points is the set of orbits. There is a functor $\pi:\mathcal F\to h_Q$ over $\mathit{Sch}/k$, uniquely specified by requiring its value on each $x\in\mathcal F(T)$ with $e(x)=(E,u)$ to pull back along $E\to T$ to $q u$. For every algebraic space $B/k$, restriction to the trivial torsors gives a bijection between maps $\mathcal F\to B$ and $G$-invariant maps $J\to B$, under which precomposition with $\pi$ corresponds to precomposition with $q$. For every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$, the presentation identifies isomorphism classes in $\mathcal F(\Omega)$ with $J(\Omega)/G(\Omega)$, and $\pi$ induces the specified bijection to $Q(\Omega)$. Thus $(Q,\pi)$ is a coarse moduli scheme in the precise algebraic-space universal and geometric-isomorphism-class sense of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. No assertion of projectivity, finite type, stack algebraicity or existence of $q$ is made.

source.place: Tag 04UV (section-group-quotient-stacks), torsor description; groupoids-quotients.tex Tags 048F (lemma-invariant) and 048J (definition-categorical). Agent expansion: descent to algebraic spaces on Zariski trivializing covers and comparison of geometric isomorphism classes.

proof.text: Work first with the presented torsor groupoid $\mathcal P$. Regard an algebraic space $B$ as its fppf sheaf. By the Zariski-covering lemma, every open trivializing cover of a torsor is an fppf cover. The equalizer in the definition of a sheaf therefore says that compatible elements of $B(U_i)$ glue uniquely in $B(T)$, and that equality in $B(T)$ can be checked on this cover. Yoneda identifies $B(T)$ with maps $h_T\to B$. This also applies with $B=h_Q$, since a scheme is its representable algebraic space. No separation hypothesis on $B$ is used.

source.place: Tag 025Y (definition-algebraic-space); sites.tex Tag 00VM (definition-sheaf-sets); topologies.tex Tag 021N (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf); categories.tex Tag 001P (lemma-yoneda).

proof.text: For $x:T\to J$ write $P_x=(G\times_k T,u_x)$ with $u_x(h,t)=h\cdot x(t)$. For any torsor pair $(E,u)$ choose a trivializing open cover $U_i$ and its identity sections $s_i:U_i\to E$. On an overlap, the $i$-th trivialization expresses $s_j$ uniquely as $g_{ij}\cdot s_i$: explicitly $g_{ij}$ is the first coordinate of $s_j$ in $E|_{U_i}\cong G\times_kU_i$. This is a morphism of schemes, so equivariance gives $u s_j=g_{ij}\cdot(u s_i)$ as morphisms. For every invariant $f:J\to B$ it follows that $f u s_j=f u s_i$. The same coordinate formula compares any two choices of sections, on a common refinement of their open covers.

source.place: Tag 04UV (section-group-quotient-stacks), objects and morphisms; elementary calculation with the Zariski trivializations stipulated in the item.

proof.text: Glue the local elements $f u s_i\in B(U_i)$ by step 1 and call the result $A_f(E,u)\in B(T)$. The common-refinement calculation in step 2 and uniqueness of gluing make it independent of the cover and sections. If $p:E\to T$, then $p^*A_f(E,u)=f u$: on $E|_{U_i}=G\times_kU_i$ the assertion is exactly $f(h\cdot u s_i)=f u s_i$, and these opens cover $E$. Conversely, any element with this pullback restricts along every $s_i$ to $f u s_i$, so it equals $A_f(E,u)$. This proves existence and uniqueness for each torsor pair, including an empty base via the empty-cover equalizer.

source.place: Tag 00VM (definition-sheaf-sets), unique gluing; examples-stacks.tex Tag 04UV (section-group-quotient-stacks), restricted to the specified Zariski trivializations.

proof.text: For a morphism $(E',u')\to(E,u)$ over $v:T'\to T$, the torsor isomorphism $E'\cong T'\times_TE$ pulls the sections $s_i$ back to sections over $v^{-1}U_i$. There $v^*A_f(E,u)$ and $A_f(E',u')$ both equal the pullback of $f u s_i$; hence they agree by the equalizer. Thus $A_f$ is a functor over the base from $\mathcal P$ to the discrete fibred groupoid $B$. Identities and composition hold because there is only one target arrow above a given base map when the section equality holds. In particular, torsor automorphisms cause no ambiguity.

source.place: Tag 04UV (section-group-quotient-stacks), description of morphisms as pullback torsor isomorphisms; sites.tex Tag 00VM (definition-sheaf-sets).

proof.text: Conversely let $A:\mathcal P\to B$ be a functor over the base. Restrict to $P_x$ for all $T$ and $x:T\to J$. The pullback compatibility of this family and Yoneda give a unique map $f:J\to B$ with $A(P_x)=f x$. To prove invariance as morphisms, take $T=G\times_kJ$, $x$ its $J$-projection and $g$ its $G$-projection. There is an isomorphism $P_x\to P_{g\cdot x}$ given by $(h,t)\mapsto(hg(t)^{-1},t)$, since $(hg^{-1})\cdot(g\cdot x)=h\cdot x$. Applying $A$ to this isomorphism gives $f x=f(g\cdot x)$ in $B(G\times_kJ)$, which is precisely invariance.

source.place: Tag 001P (lemma-yoneda); examples-stacks.tex Tag 04UV (section-group-quotient-stacks), proof of proposition-equal-quotient-stacks, the right-translation-by-inverse formula.

proof.text: These constructions are inverse. Starting with invariant $f$, the global identity section of $P_x$ gives $A_f(P_x)=f x$, so restriction recovers $f$. Starting with $A$, each $s_i$ gives an isomorphism $P_{u s_i}\to(E,u)|_{U_i}$, $(h,t)\mapsto h\cdot s_i(t)$. Functoriality of $A$ then gives $A(E,u)|_{U_i}=f u s_i$. Unique gluing implies $A=A_f$ on objects and hence on arrows. Precomposition by the given cartesian equivalence $e:\mathcal F\to\mathcal P$ is also a bijection on these functors: a quasi-inverse gives its inverse, and its unit and counit become identities after mapping to a discrete groupoid. Thus the same correspondence holds for $\mathcal F$. It is independent of choices, and natural in $B$, since composing $f$ with $B\to B'$ gives the same local sections as composing $A_f$.

source.place: Tag 04UV (section-group-quotient-stacks), torsor trivialization and equivariant morphisms; sites.tex Tag 00VM (definition-sheaf-sets). Elementary inverse and equivalence calculations.

proof.text: Apply the construction to the invariant map $q:J\to Q$, using the representable algebraic space $h_Q$, and put $\pi=A_qe$. Step 3 proves the required identity after pullback to $E$ and its uniqueness. For $b:Q\to B$, the functor $b\pi$ restricts on $P_x$ to $bqx$, so under step 6 precomposition with $\pi$ is exactly $b\mapsto bq$. The assumed categorical bijection for $q$ and the bijection in step 6 therefore give the algebraic-space universal property for $\pi$.

source.place: Tag 048J (definition-categorical), universal property applied as an explicit hypothesis; examples-stacks.tex Tag 04UV (section-group-quotient-stacks).

proof.text: Let $\Omega/k$ be algebraically closed. Any open cover of the nonempty one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ contains its whole base, so every Zariski locally trivial torsor over it has a section $s$. The isomorphism $(h,t)\mapsto h\cdot s(t)$ identifies its pair with $P_x$, where $x=u(s)\in J(\Omega)$. Replacing $s$ by $g\cdot s$ replaces $x$ by $g\cdot x$. Every equivariant isomorphism $P_x\to P_y$ is right multiplication by its value $a\in G(\Omega)$ at the identity, and commuting with the maps to $J$ says $x=a\cdot y$. Conversely this equation defines such an isomorphism. Thus isomorphism classes are precisely $J(\Omega)/G(\Omega)$; the equivalence $e$ preserves and reflects these classes. The value of $\pi$ on this class is $q(x)$ by step 3, hence is the assumed bijection to $Q(\Omega)$. Together with step 7 this is exactly the coarse definition.
